title: Retry with exponential backoff for flaky API calls

pattern.problem: API calls to external services intermittently fail due to rate limits, temporary outages, or network issues. Simple retry loops either fail too fast or waste time with fixed delays.
pattern.approach: Implement exponential backoff with jitter: start with a short delay, double it on each retry, and add random jitter to prevent thundering herd. Cap the maximum delay and total retry count.
pattern.when_to_use: Any time you call an external API that might be rate-limited, temporarily unavailable, or experience transient network errors. Especially important for CI/CD pipelines, data pipelines, and background jobs.
pattern.when_not_to_use: Don't use for errors that won't resolve with retries (authentication failures, 404s, validation errors). Don't use for user-facing synchronous requests where you need immediate feedback — show an error instead of making the user wait.

solution.description: The exponential backoff pattern increases wait time between retries exponentially (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, ...) with random jitter to avoid synchronized retry storms. Most HTTP client libraries have built-in support: Python's tenacity, JavaScript's axios-retry, Go's backoff package.
